explanation: Use a depth-first stack of nodes and open lower/upper bounds inherited from ancestors. The initial sentinels lie outside all signed 32-bit keys. Tighten the upper bound for a left child and the lower bound for a right child.
correctness: Each bound summarizes every relevant ancestor restriction. Passing the current key as the new bound enforces all descendant restrictions inductively.
walkthrough: For [10,4,16,1,7,12,19], node 4 inherits an upper bound of 10; its right child 7 must lie strictly between 4 and 10. Node 16 inherits a lower bound of 10, and its left child 12 must lie between 10 and 16. Every inherited interval is respected, so the answer is true.
edgeCases: A left descendant exceeding the root fails even if its immediate parent comparison succeeds; duplicate keys also fail. Signed 32-bit endpoints are valid keys.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: each node is checked once against two inherited bounds.
spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary space for pending branches or recursive frames along tree height h; O(n) on a skewed tree.
